summary: The new ML-path placebo comparison is correctly wired to the intended files and performs a strict pair-and-field equality check. The main defect is that any misspelled mode silently runs the original Ancestry placebo, potentially reporting success while leaving the ML path unchecked.

findings.title: A misspelled ML mode silently validates the Ancestry path instead
findings.what_the_code_does: The script initializes the baseline filenames and changes them only under `if "`mode'"=="ml"`. Every other nonempty argument—including a typo such as `m1` or `ML`—therefore selects `link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` and the original placebo rather than rejecting the invocation.
findings.why_it_matters: A mistyped command can print `PLACEBO PASSED` while never testing the newly added FamilySearch-1930 plus ML-1940 path. This creates false assurance about the comparability check supporting the slides result.
findings.how_to_check: Run `do MATCHING/check_placebo.do m1` and inspect the first displayed filename; it will identify the Ancestry paper link rather than stop with an invalid-argument error.
findings.suggested_fix: Before choosing filenames, require the mode to be exactly empty or `ml`, and exit with error 198 for any other value. Optionally normalize case if `ML` should be accepted.

verified_clean.item: The documented ML invocation maps to the intended mixed-path output and paper ML link.
verified_clean.evidence: `MATCHING/check_placebo.do:13-18` documents the nine-argument matching command, while `MATCHING/check_placebo.do:25-27` selects `link1930_1940_true_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` and `link1930_1940_fsplacebo1930_ml1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta`. The latter naming convention is generated by `MATCHING/3_append_and_clean_all_links_christian_torbenV2.do:80-81,141`.

verified_clean.item: The comparison detects missing or extra link pairs rather than allowing merge mismatches to pass silently.
verified_clean.evidence: `MATCHING/check_placebo.do:33,42-50` establishes unique pair keys on both inputs, tabulates the merge, counts every `_merge!=3` observation, and marks the check as failed when any exist.

verified_clean.item: The comparison checks all stated link attributes after matching pairs.
verified_clean.evidence: `MATCHING/check_placebo.do:34-35,52-59` compares the conservative-band flag, both names in both years, and both middle initials, then exits with status 9 if any field differs.

verified_clean.item: Blank strings and numeric missing values do not inflate a reported agreement rate in this test.
verified_clean.evidence: `MATCHING/check_placebo.do:52-55` is an exact parity test using inequality, not an accuracy or agreement-rate calculation; equal blanks or equal missing values are appropriately treated as identical file contents.

verified_clean.item: The script remains read-only with respect to permanent project and data outputs.
verified_clean.evidence: `MATCHING/check_placebo.do:37-38` writes only a Stata `tempfile`; the remainder of the script loads, merges, counts, displays, and exits without saving a permanent dataset.

verified_clean.item: The untracked review artifacts introduce no executable analysis or identification change.
verified_clean.evidence: `review/reports/2026-11-14_152410-working-prompt.md:1-39` records the review prompt, and `review/revision-notes-2026-11-13.md:1-18` contains draft-review notes rather than executable calculations.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code could not be assessed against manuscript language; the untracked revision notes are not a substitute for the draft.
The external census and multi-gigabyte linkage datasets were unavailable, so the placebo comparison and matching pipeline could not be executed.
Stata was not run; runtime conclusions are based on source tracing and documented Stata semantics.
This was a diff-scoped review of the uncommitted working tree, not a full audit of the matching pipeline or the identification strategy behind the paper's estimands.
